newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr ends little changed after earnings data.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr ends little changed after earnings data.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed and near the bottom of its range on Tuesday, with only muted reaction to key earnings data.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6964/71, up from 0.6970/77 at the open, but firmed to 68.63 from 68.57 on its Trade-Weighted Index as the U.S. dollar firmed against the mark and yen.

Statistics New Zealand said total average hourly ordinary time earnings rose 0.7 percent in the November 1996 quarter and 3.5 percent for the year, while the corresponding private sector figures were 0.6 percent and 3.8 percent.
Most economists described the figures as neutral, but Bankers Trust said recent data had increased the risk the Reserve Bank of New Zealand would tighten sooner rather than later.

Dealers said the data prompted a slight mark-up in the Kiwi, but it ran into selling around 0.6980. There was some offshore selling, too, in the high 0.6960s, and Australian dollar weakness was another negative for the currency.
"The Aussie faded a bit today and dragged the Kiwi down," one dealer said.
There was some talk of further Eurokiwi issues being priced following a NZ$100 million five-year issue announced overnight by lead manager Hambros on behalf of KFW International Finance.
Dealers saw support holding around 0.6950 and a trading range of around 0.6945-85 for the next couple of days.
